rows.control: Row action 'Acknowledge' on an OPEN incident (accessible name carries the incident title)
rows.scope: One incident row, named in the button's accessible name and tooltip; stays open and reassignable

confirmation.reason: Acknowledging marks an incident as seen by an operator and nothing else: it stays OPEN-equivalent (ACKNOWLEDGED), can still be resolved or reassigned, has no external, billing, evidence, custody or customer effect, and is limited to the row the operator is looking at. A dialog on every acknowledgement would be pure confirmation fatigue on the most frequent triage click.

rows.control: Row action 'Assign to me' / 'Unassign' on an incident (accessible name carries the incident title)
rows.scope: One incident row's assignee; the operator themself or nobody; named in the button's accessible name

confirmation.reason: Assigning an incident to yourself, or returning it to the unassigned queue, is immediately reversible by the same button, affects only the visible row, and has no external, billing, evidence, custody, security or customer consequence. It is the operator's own work-claim, not a decision about the condition.

rows.control: Row action 'Verify' on a custody attestation (accessible name carries the attestation and evidence ids)
rows.scope: One attestation of the active workspace is re-checked against its custody event; a report is shown; nothing is written

confirmation.reason: Verification recomputes and displays a report for one attestation; the handler writes no row, changes no evidence, custody, TSA or report state, and reaches no external provider. Running it twice returns the same report. It is a read expressed as POST because it carries a workspace-scoped body, and a confirmation dialog would add a step to an action that changes nothing.

rows.control: Button 'Verify reproducibility' in the export drawer
rows.scope: One export of the active workspace, named in the drawer header; a report is computed and shown, an INFO/WARNING security event is recorded, nothing is written to the export

confirmation.reason: Reproducibility verification recomputes the export's manifest hash and compares it; the export, its artifacts and retention are not modified, no provider is called, and repeating it produces the same report (only an informational security event per run). The report is the point of the action and a dialog before a read-only check would add nothing an operator could decide.

cells.reason: This row never existed as a behaviour. /admin/customers/:id calls `/v1/admin/orgs/${id}/${leg}` where leg is 'suspend' | 'resume'; the earlier inventory truncated the template at the interpolation and pattern-matched the remainder against POST /v1/admin/orgs/:id/plan — a plan mutation this page has never issued (the real plan grant lives on /admin/provisioning and is PATCH). The inventory now expands the union declared on `leg`, so the phantom plan row is replaced by the two real lifecycle mutations, each carrying a full row of required cells.

cells.control: Button 'Probe health' in the signer drawer
cells.scope: One signer, read only
cells.reason: Not a mutation. The page calls GET /v1/operations/signers/:id/health (registered as app.get, emits an INFO security event and writes nothing). The earlier inventory matched the page's `/${action}` template against the first two-parameter registration under /signers, which was this GET probe, and listed it as a POST — while hiding the three real POSTs (promote, retire, revoke) that the template actually sends. The inventory now expands the union declared on the parameter, so the health probe leaves the matrix and the three lifecycle mutations enter it with every cell required.
